gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-stack-sans-headl: Stack Sans Headline reads friendly and crisp, with a deep middle band and one unvarying line throughout. Stack Sans Headline would carry a long page without tiring the eye, while Stencilia stays up top looking structural.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-stack-sans-notch: Striking is Stencilia's whole manner, with gaps left open at every curve end. Stack Sans Notch follows in rod-stock lines and generous lowercase, so the heading makes its entrance and the text simply gets on with it.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-sulphur-point: Sulphur Point reads like a sans-serif drawn with a marker, its bulky lowercase showing distinct gaps in the a and s. Stencilia stays sharper and more structural above it.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-tiktok-sans: Modern is the first impression of Stencilia, structural and striking with its compact gap below the ascender line. TikTok Sans takes over underneath, its x-height climbing nearly to cap height, so the text feels large and the heading stays the showpiece.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-ubuntu-sans: Ubuntu Sans looks like bent copper pipe, with washer-sized eyes on every lowercase letter. Its single-stroke brush look at constant width sits against Stencilia's structural, striking display shapes, and that gap in character is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans draws every curve as if with a ruler. Its tall x-height fills the line and its terminals stay wide open, so a long page feels steady beneath Stencilia's striking heading.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-yaldevi: Yaldevi reads cleanly, its e opening clearly to the right and its lowercase running oversized. And Stencilia handles the drama above, leaving that sans to speak plainly beneath it.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-abeezee: Stentiga spreads its letters out with luxurious tracking and crossbars as thick as its stems. And ABeeZee, with a high mean line and terminals finishing clear of the stem, gives the text a friendlier footing.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-aldrich: Aldrich has an x-height near its cap height and round letters that look cupped, as if tracing one thick thread. Stentiga does the refined, spread-out showpiece work, and the sans-serif body handles the steady running text.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-alexandria: Stentiga's line never varies in thickness, and its openings gape like a door left ajar. Alexandria follows with wide terminals on a tall body, so the sans-serif text feels as open as the heading.
